e: From Latin duumvirātus, from duumvir + -ātus. Equivalent to duumvir + -ate (forms nouns denoting rank or office, here the group of people involved with it).
q: To replace the all-powerful Salan, de Gaulle appointed a duumvirate – Paul Delouvrier and General Maurice Challe.
1977, Alistair Horne, A Savage War of Peace, New York: Review Books, published 2006, page 310:
This was to raise the prospect of a duumvirate – ‘two heads in the same hat’, as Bernis quaintly put it.
